response.full_narrative:
Dawn (06:01:00) in the Misty Mountain Pass—the chill air bites at your skin as you stand near the jagged edge of the trail, the world around you a shifting sea of gray and white. You peer through the veil, narrowing your eyes as the first pale light of the new year filters through the high peaks of the Spine of the World. 

As you hold your breath, your ears pick up a rhythmic scratching sound—not the whistling wind, but the distinct rasp of stone on stone—coming from a narrow ledge just below the path. Through a sudden rift in the mist, you catch the flickering silhouette of something small and hunched moving near a cluster of jagged rocks. It hasn't seen you yet, but the sound suggests it is digging for something—or perhaps sharpening a blade. The scent of damp earth and old pine is heavy in the air.
